name: Godescalcus
dates: dates not given in the source
bio: J. M. Neale describes Godescalcus as the most famous writer, next to S. Notker himself, of the Proses named from Notker, and warns that he is not to be confused with his predestinarian namesake. Neale gives no dates for him.

This file gives Neale's verse translation of the Alleluiatic Sequence 'Cantemus cuncti', which he says was written for the Deposition of Alleluia at Septuagesima and which he first translated for the Hymnal Noted (Mediaeval Hymns and Sequences, 1867). His other two versions of Godescalcus are literal prose and are not included.

poems.title: The strain upraise of joy and praise, Alleluia
poems.author: Godescalcus
poems.text:
The strain upraise of joy and praise, Alleluia.

To the glory of their King
Shall the ransom'd people sing Alleluia.

And the Choirs that dwell on high
Shall re-echo through the sky Alleluia.

They through the fields of Paradise that roam,
The blessed ones, repeat through that bright home  Alleluia.

The planets glittering on their heavenly way,
The shining constellations, join, and say Alleluia.

Ye clouds that onward sweep!
Ye winds on pinions light!
Ye thunders, echoing loud and deep!
Ye lightnings, wildly bright!
In sweet consent unite your Alleluia.

Ye floods and ocean billows!
Ye storms and winter snow!
Ye days of cloudless beauty!
Hoar frost and summer glow!
Ye groves that wave in spring,
And glorious forests, sing  Alleluia.

First let the birds, with painted plumage gay,
Exalt their great Creator's praise, and say  Alleluia.

Then let the beasts of earth with varying strain,
Join in Creation's Hymn, and cry again  Alleluia.

Thou jubilant abyss of ocean, cry  Alleluia.
Ye tracts of earth and continents, reply  Alleluia.

To God, Who all Creation made,
The frequent hymn be duly paid:  Alleluia.

Now from all men be outpour'd
Alleluia to the Lord;
With Alleluia evermore
The Son and Spirit we adore.

Praise be done to the Three in One.
Alleluia! Alleluia! Alleluia! Alleluia!
